title: The Summit Club
clue: Your highest point doesn't need to be very high to count.
reveal: Find the highest point you can comfortably reach together: a rise, a footbridge, a bench on a bank. Spot it the day before, agree a turnaround rule, and reach it in ten to twenty minutes from home. Every summit goes into an open-ended register jar.
objective: Reach a comfortable high point near home at your dog's pace, pause for the view and add a named summit to your register jar.
instructions: The day before, spot your summit: the highest point within an easy walk, such as a rise at the end of the street, a footbridge, a bench on a bank or the top of a gentle slope. Look at it from where you stand and say, that one is ours. Check for steep edges and leash rules.

Agree the turnaround rule out loud: if either of you is tired, worried or simply done, the summit is wherever you are standing and it counts in full. Your dog's exit is built in: a sit, a lie-down or a turn toward home is a vote for summiting right here.
Go at a cool time with water and a loose leash. Walk at your dog's pace and stop for every sniff, with no time limit; the sniffing is the climb.
At the top, offer water and then do nothing for five minutes. Let your dog sniff, look or lie down while you look at the view and find your own home in it.
Name your summit and give it an altitude measured in something your dog does, such as twelve sniffs high. It is a joke, not a count.
Take the way down slowly on the easiest ground, and stop wherever your dog wants to.
At home, write the summit's name, its altitude and the date on a slip of paper, fold it and drop it in the Summit Register, any jar or tin. The jar never gets full; it is simply where summits live.
twist: Height is measured in sniffs, wherever you turn around counts in full, and every summit goes in a jar with no total to reach.
variations: No hill nearby, or a slow day: your summit is the top-floor window, a balcony, the top step or the highest bench. Sit with the view for five minutes and name it.
Senior, small or stiff dog: choose the smallest rise on the flattest surface, go in cool hours, and ask your vet which slopes suit your dog. Going around instead of up is a fine answer.
Seated or limited-mobility owner: choose a level viewpoint with a smooth path and a bench, and let the summit be the bench.

Landmark day, the bigger version (needs a car or bus): a hill, viewpoint or woodland trail by foot, bus or car. Check dog and leash rules, closures and nesting seasons first, and pause at three landmarks, such as a big tree, water and open sky, before the top. Restrain your dog in the car.
completion: You have reached your summit or your agreed turnaround, sat for a moment and named it.
photoIdea: The view from the top with your dog's back or paws at the edge of the frame, taken while they sniff.
memoryPrompt: What is your summit called, and how many sniffs high was it?
supplies: Paper and a pen for the register slip
optionalSupplies: A jar or tin for the register
substitutes: No jar: an envelope or a mug works as the register

reservation.note: The core is on foot and needs nothing booked. The landmark-day version needs a car or bus; check dog and leash rules and closures first.

safety: Sidewalk too hot for the back of your hand is too hot for paws; head home if your dog pants hard or shivers.
Keep your dog on a leash near drops and edges, take the way down slowly, and leave wildlife alone.
Restrain your dog in the car, check for ticks afterwards, and ask your vet what suits an older or stiff dog.
